newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 1.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Transnet chairman Louise Tager suspended controversial Portnet executive Sipho Nyawo on Thursday -- after intervention by Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau -- as allegations of misconduct and credit card fraud mounted.

- Financial Services group Capital Alliance has secured sufficient financing to buy a 35 percent shareholding in mining house JCI Ltd from Anglo American, say sources close to the bid. The interest is worth 2.6 billion rand based on JCI's market capitalisation on Thursday.

- Zulu king Goodwill Zwelithini transferred authority of land falling under the Ingonyama Trust Act to KwaZulu-Natal premier Frand Mdlalose on Thursday in a bid to pave the way for development in the Durban metropolitan council and transitional local councils.

- A massive increase in black employees in government was evidence that affirmative action programmes in national departments had been successful, the Central Statistical Services said in an analysis of racial trends in the public service released on Thursday.

- Sipho Nyawo, the suspended Transnet executive director, denied on Thursday that he owed Strategic Planning Institute (SPI), a company that is a services supplier to Portnet, the port authority that falls under his management. Nyawo was suspended by Louise Tager, the chairman of Transnet, on the order of Stella Sigcau, the public enterprises minister, after the allegation was published in the Beeld on Thursday.

- Rob Lee, the hard-hitting chief economist of Old Mutual in the 1980s and now an economic consultant for BOE Natwest, will leave South Africa in January to settle with his family in Scotland, where he was born.
- Strong second-half catches helped Sea Harvest shrug off losses from its Namibian associate and net a satisfactory 17 percent increase in earnings to 57.6 million rand in the year to September 30.

- The appointment of Mike King, the finance director of Anglo American, to Johnnic's board signals that Anglo will not take its new business partnership with the National Empowerment Consortium lightly.

- They thought they were going to Botswana for military training by the ANC. But the 10 young Mamelodi activists were led to their execution by a combined security police and military hit squad. The story of the Nietverdiend 10 was told to a stunned Truth and Reconciliation Commission amnesty hearing on Thursday by one of the executioners, Brigadier Jack Cronje, former commander of the Northern Transvaal security branch.

- There is uncertainty about whether murderer Eugene de Kock will qualify for parole. In passing sentence in the Pretoria Supreme Court on Wednesday, Mr Justice Willem van der Merwe said that under no circumstances could anyone who was sentenced to more than 100 years qualify for parole. De Kock was given two life sentences plus 212 years.
